solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Early stage shoe's warmer

parts.note: a heat is an early qualifying round of a race or competition
a pump is a light slip-on shoe

explanation.surface: Some footwear in its first phase is said to be the cosy kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's simply links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A heat pump is a device that warms a building by drawing heat from outside air or ground.

clue.text: American in hotel twice finished whitewash

indicators.note: the American letters go between the two hotel letters

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
twice supplies the hotel letter a second time
US means American
up means over or finished, as in 'time's up'

explanation.surface: An American booked into a hotel two times, finished off a cover-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To whitewash a scandal is to conceal it, to hush it up.

clue.text: Affair involves head of Royal Mail perhaps

indicators.note: contains, so the affair word wraps round the picked letter

parts.note: an amour is a love affair

indicators.note: takes the first letter of Royal

explanation.surface: A love affair implicates the boss of the Royal Mail postal service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royal Mail' reads as the British postal service, but Mail is chain mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Chain mail is a type of protective body covering, so it is an example of armour.

clue.text: Corrective system of exercising alone with CD playing

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercising at school

indicators.note: the letters play about and fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remedial workout regime done solo with a music disc spinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' is the anagram signal, rearranging ALONE and CD; PE is the British school abbreviation for physical education.
explanation.definitionFit: A penal code is the body of laws setting out crimes and their punishments, a system for correcting offenders.

clue.text: Wrongly deliver small part of speech among timid types

indicators.note: puts the small and the pronoun letters within the timid types

parts.note: mice stand for timid, mousy people
a pronoun is one of the parts of speech in grammar

explanation.surface: A shy group fumble the delivery of a brief grammatical item.
explanation.definitionFit: To mispronounce is to say a word incorrectly, so it is to deliver it wrongly in speech.

clue.text: Baby, curiously, last to go in church

indicators.note: says the trimmed word sits inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: the final letter of the synonym is dropped, as the last one leaves

parts.note: oddly means curiously or strangely

explanation.surface: A strange baby, it seems, with the final one leaving the church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baby' looks like a noun but is the verb: ODDLY loses its Y ('last to go') to give ODDL, which goes 'in' CE.
explanation.definitionFit: To baby someone is to pamper or mollycoddle them, which is exactly what coddling means.

clue.text: Old police company, climbing, come to pass

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the letters read upwards

parts.note: the RUC, Royal Ulster Constabulary, was Northern Ireland's former police force

explanation.surface: A former police firm rising up and then happening.
explanation.walkthrough: The RUC was replaced in 2001, hence 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: To occur is to happen or take place, which is what to come to pass means.

clue.text: Performed first part of play cold? That's edifying

parts.note: did means performed or carried out
Act I is the opening section of a stage play
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Acting the opening of a drama in a chill: how improving.
explanation.definitionFit: Didactic means intended to teach or instruct, much as edifying means morally improving.

clue.text: Can I get through dance?

definitions.meaning: the polite phrase asking someone to let you pass
a dance in which one may cut in on a couple

explanation.surface: Asking a partner whether one may cut in on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The polite request to pass is this phrase, and a ballroom dance where partners can be claimed bears the same name.

clue.text: Monotony of chaps in rough seas bearing south

indicators.note: places the chaps inside the scrambled seas
rough seas are churned up, so the letters of seas are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
chaps are men
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Sailors find life dull out on choppy water heading southwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' turns SEAS into SAES, MEN goes 'in' it (SAMENES), and S is added on at the end ('bearing').
explanation.definitionFit: Monotony is a dull lack of variety, the quality of everything being alike.

clue.text: Cutting from papers I found in a volume

indicators.note: puts the papers and I inside the volume abbreviation

parts.note: cc, cubic centimetres, is a measure of volume
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: A newspaper clipping taken from documents and tucked into a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' suggests a press clipping, but it is the definition, meaning sharp or biting.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidic remarks are sharp and biting, the same sense as cutting remarks.

clue.text: EEC high flier stealing my French and German cash once

indicators.note: the high flier takes in the other pieces, so they go inside it

parts.note: a comet flies high across the sky
mon is French for my
the mark was Germany's currency before the euro

explanation.surface: A rising star in the European bloc pockets old francs and marks.
explanation.walkthrough: MONMARK goes inside COMET after COM. EEC stands for the European Economic Community.
explanation.definitionFit: The EEC, the forerunner of the European Union, was popularly known in Britain by this name.

clue.text: The British oddly unable to follow routine

indicators.note: the picked letters come after the pronoun

parts.note: said by Britons, 'the British' is us

indicators.note: takes the first, third and fifth letters of the word unable

explanation.surface: The British, strangely, are incapable of keeping to a set routine.
explanation.walkthrough: US here is the pronoun 'we' as the British would say it of themselves, not the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Routine as an adjective means ordinary or customary, which is what usual means.

clue.text: Cheats go round following drivers for top car parts

indicators.note: the cheats' letters surround the following and drivers pieces

parts.note: to rook someone is to swindle them, so rooks are cheats
f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
the RAC, Royal Automobile Club, is a British motorists' organisation

explanation.surface: Swindlers circle behind motorists as they make for the best bits of a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drivers' is the RAC, the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation roughly like the AAA in the US; ROOKS is the verb sense of cheating.
explanation.definitionFit: Roof racks are frames fitted on the roof of a car for carrying luggage, so they are parts on its top.

clue.text: Roaming at night, numb Somalis staggered miles

indicators.note: staggering is lurching about unsteadily, so these letters are thrown into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Some numbed Somalis wandered after dark, tottering for miles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staggered' rearranges NUMBSOMALIS into SOMNAMBULIS; M for miles then completes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Somnambulism is sleepwalking, wandering about in one's sleep, typically at night.

clue.text: To perform subtly, felt maybe piano should intervene

indicators.note: the piano letter must come between letters of the felt word

parts.note: felt is one material used as underlay beneath carpets
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: An actor told to tone it down, with a piano coming between.
explanation.walkthrough: 'felt' looks like the past of feel, but it is the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: To underplay a role is to act it with restraint, deliberately understated.

clue.text: Repulsive joint found in prison, half of it missing

indicators.note: puts the joint inside what is left of the prison
only one of the two equal halves of the prison name is kept

parts.note: Sing Sing is a famous prison in New York State
the hock is the joint in an animal's hind leg

explanation.surface: A disgusting cut of meat discovered in a jail, half gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a dive or a cannabis joint, both at home in a prison, but here it is the leg joint HOCK, placed in SING.
explanation.definitionFit: Shocking can mean extremely offensive or disgusting, close in sense to repulsive.

clue.text: Arrest guy stupidly wasting first of government funds

indicators.note: done foolishly, so the letters are jumbled into a new order
losing, so the picked letter is taken away from the pool
takes the opening letter of government

explanation.surface: Detain the fellow who idiotically squanders public money.
explanation.walkthrough: From the letters of ARREST GUY, 'wasting first of government' removes a G; 'stupidly' rearranges the remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The treasury is a state's store of money, or the department that manages public finances.

clue.text: Theatre regularly left Bill filling horsey pantomime part

indicators.note: takes every other letter of theatre, starting from the second
the bill goes into the middle of the horsey word

parts.note: equine means horsey, relating to horses
an ad, advertisement, is a bill or poster

explanation.surface: A theatre bill featuring a pantomime horse scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks HAR from Theatre; then AD goes 'filling' EQUINE to make EQUINADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A harlequinade is the part of a traditional pantomime in which Harlequin and the clown play the leading roles.

clue.text: Bunch of flyers, doubly good in strong wind

indicators.note: the two letters sit inside the wind word

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind
doubly supplies the good letter a second time

explanation.surface: A flock of birds, twice as fine, flying into a fierce wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaggle is a flock of geese, here called flyers because they take to the air.

clue.text: Bust university acquired by nation

indicators.note: taken in, so the university letter goes inside the nation word

parts.note: a state is a nation

explanation.surface: A broke university is taken over by the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' looks like 'broke', but is the noun: a sculpted head.
explanation.definitionFit: A bust is a sculpture of a head and shoulders, a kind of statue.

clue.text: Teas and coffee putting paid to second dance

parts.note: cha is tea, so two teas are cha cha

indicators.note: ending or getting rid of the second inside the coffee word

parts.note: mocha is a kind of coffee
mo is a moment, a second, as in 'half a mo'

explanation.surface: Tea and coffee served, but the second cup is cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA is British slang for tea; MOCHA without MO, the informal 'moment', leaves the last CHA.
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha-cha is a Latin American ballroom dance of Cuban origin.

clue.text: There's nothing exceptional holding in this opening feature

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer within its letters, spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A doorway's fitting is remarkable for nothing in particular.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'notHING Exceptional'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinge is the pivot that lets a door, gate or lid open, a characteristic part of any opening.

clue.text: Pan, and what may be in it?

definitions.meaning: to pan a play is to criticise it harshly
a ... joint of meat cooks in a ... pan

explanation.surface: A kitchen pan and whatever is cooking inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition depends on the first: the 'it' is a pan in its kitchen sense, while the word itself is the verb of critics.
explanation.definitionFit: Critics who savage a show pan or roast it, and a roast is a joint of meat cooked in a tin.

clue.text: Reptile, one to the fore in S American region

indicators.note: the one is moved from its place to the front of the word

parts.note: Guiana is a region on the north coast of South America
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lizard, the leading specimen in a South American territory.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the I of GUIANA to the front ('to the fore') turns it into the lizard.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguana is a large tropical American lizard, so it is a kind of reptile.

clue.text: Through which to view star?

parts.note: suggests a telescope or theatre box, but means a roof window opening on the night sky

explanation.surface: Where would you look to see a celebrity?
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' hints at a celebrity glimpsed from a stage door, but it is the celestial kind, seen through a window in the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A skylight is a window set in a roof or ceiling, through which the heavens can be seen.

clue.text: Mentioned chap's hot tourist attraction

indicators.note: spoken of, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a geezer is British slang for a chap or bloke; the 's stands for 'is' and joins the definition

explanation.surface: That bloke spoken of is a sizzling draw for visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech GEYSER is often said like GEEZER, slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A geyser is a hot spring that spouts boiling water, like Old Faithful, drawing crowds of sightseers.

clue.text: Gas initially envelops your old tip, according to reports

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of envelops

parts.note: thy is the old form of your

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to tip is to lean or tilt

explanation.surface: A gas first wraps your ancient rubbish dump, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' looks like a British rubbish dump; here it is the verb, LEAN, written LENE by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethylene is a flammable hydrocarbon gas used in plastics and to ripen fruit.
